This documents an original commitment to contribute annually 1% of gross gaming revenue, with a stated minimum annual amount, from opening. However, the stated minimum amount in the excerpt is $12.5 million, not $15 million.

c2.excerpt: 3. Will Bally’s provide all operational support including but not limited to staffing, accounting, and legal support to this board through the Bally’s Foundation and, if necessary, create a Bronx- specific arm of the Foundation to administer and help facilitate the local Community Benefit Funds? c3.title: https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/final-draft-cac-proposal-and-amendments-for-ballys-bronx-casino-and-resort-baly-response-9.19.2025.pdf
c3.excerpt: Community Benefit Fund Contributions and Priorities 1. Will Bally’s commit to contributing a minimum of seventeen and a half million dollars annually, or one percent of gross gaming revenue, whichever is higher, beginning at the time of licensure rather than waiting until the facility opens? We commit to an annual contribution of 1% of gross gaming revenue with a minimum of $12.5 million from the time the gaming facility is opened. We would highlight that this is a minimum commitment to fund solely the Community Benefit Fund, not inclusive of additional commitments.

c5.title: https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/final-draft-cac-proposal-and-amendments-for-ballys-bronx-casino-and-resort-baly-response-9.19.2025.pdf
c5.excerpt: 3. Will all distributions be transparent, with public annual reports and presentations to the community? Yes, all distributions from the Community Benefit Fund will be conducted with full transparency. Gaming revenue figures, which form the basis for these distributions, are publicly reported, ensuring that the underlying financial data is accessible to all stakeholders. The calculation methods for determining fund distributions are also made public, allowing for open scrutiny and understanding of how funds are allocated. The Community Benefit Fund Board should provide comprehensive annual reports and presentations outlining the fund's financial performance, distribution outcomes, and the impact of the funded initiatives on the community.

findings.summary: In response to a request that it contribute at least $17.5 million annually or 1% of gross gaming revenue beginning at licensure, Bally’s instead said: “We commit to an annual contribution of 1% of gross gaming revenue with a minimum of $12.5 million from the time the gaming facility is opened,” and added that this was a minimum commitment solely for the Community Benefit Fund, excluding additional commitments.
findings.explanation: This passage directly states Bally’s commitment terms, timing, and that the $12.5 million/1% pledge is only for the Community Benefit Fund. It also shows Bally’s did not accept the asked-for licensure start or $17.5 million minimum in this document.
findings.excerpt: Will Bally’s commit to contributing a minimum of seventeen and a half million dollars annually, or one percent of gross gaming revenue, whichever is higher, beginning at the time of licensure rather than waiting until the facility opens? We commit to an annual contribution of 1% of gross gaming revenue with a minimum of $12.5 million from the time the gaming facility is opened. We would highlight that this is a minimum commitment to fund solely the Community Benefit Fund, not inclusive of additional commitments.

findings.summary: Bally’s said it would leave “specific funding directives” to the Community Benefit Fund Board, including discretion in selecting investments or other improvements to be made throughout the community.
findings.explanation: This supports that a Community Benefit Fund Board was contemplated to direct spending decisions, but it does not establish the board was independent/local in the exact terms stated or that it was already operating.
findings.excerpt: Will the Community Benefit Fund Board and Bally’s codify that projects and institutions within CB10, using it as the nucleus of priority, are funded first before expanding to the broader Bronx, ensuring that CB10 which will be greatly impacted by this project’s needs are fully addressed? Bally’s will leave the specific funding directives to be made by the Community Benefit Fund Board to the Board including discretion in selecting investments or other improvements to be made throughout the community.

findings.summary: Bally’s said all Community Benefit Fund distributions would be conducted with “full transparency,” with gaming revenue figures and distribution-calculation methods made public, and that the Community Benefit Fund Board “should provide comprehensive annual reports and presentations” on financial performance, distribution outcomes, and community impact.
findings.explanation: This passage documents promised transparency and an expected reporting role for the board, but the wording about board reports is aspirational ('should provide') rather than proof of actual reports or board constitution.
findings.excerpt: Will all distributions be transparent, with public annual reports and presentations to the community? Yes, all distributions from the Community Benefit Fund will be conducted with full transparency. Gaming revenue figures, which form the basis for these distributions, are publicly reported, ensuring that the underlying financial data is accessible to all stakeholders. The calculation methods for determining fund distributions are also made public, allowing for open scrutiny and understanding of how funds are allocated. The Community Benefit Fund Board should provide comprehensive annual reports and presentations outlining the fund's financial performance, distribution outcomes, and the impact of the funded initiatives on the community.

findings.summary: When asked whether Bally’s would provide operational support to the board through the Bally’s Foundation, Bally’s replied that its intention was for all functions for the Bronx Community Benefit Fund to be funded via Bally’s Bronx, and that the Bally’s Foundation is an entirely separate nonprofit not associated with the pledged Community Benefit Fund.
findings.explanation: This clarifies administration/support context: the source does not confirm that an independent local board would administer the fund through the Bally’s Foundation; instead it distinguishes the Foundation from the pledged fund.
findings.excerpt: Will Bally’s provide all operational support including but not limited to staffing, accounting, and legal support to this board through the Bally’s Foundation and, if necessary, create a Bronx- specific arm of the Foundation to administer and help facilitate the local Community Benefit Funds? Bally’s should designate a hired company representative, ideally a CB10 resident with deep knowledge of the surrounding neighborhoods, to work with the board and the community. Our intention is for all functions for the Bronx Community Benefit Fund to be funded by the Community Benefit Funds via Bally’s Bronx. Additionally, the Bally’s Foundation is an entirely separate entity (non-profit) and is not associated with the pledged Community Benefit Fund via Bally’s Bronx.

findings.summary: In a later response memo, Bally’s said: “Upon awarding of a license we will explore and define the appropriate methodology for providing the financial support for all Community Benefit Fund and associated commitments.”
findings.explanation: This later passage indicates that, at that point, Bally’s had not yet defined the methodology for providing financial support, which limits what can be concluded about final administration arrangements or implementation.
findings.excerpt: Upon awarding of a license we will explore and define the appropriate methodology for providing the financial support for all Community Benefit Fund and associated commitments.

findings.summary: Casino Reports later reported that Bally’s “raised its minimum annual commitment to the CFTB from $12.5 million to $15 million at the time of the casino opening,” while 1% of gross gaming revenue could be higher than $15 million.
findings.explanation: This is secondary-source reporting of a later increase to $15 million, matching the question’s figure, but the supplied primary-source passages do not directly document that revised term.
findings.excerpt: Bally's also raised its minimum annual commitment to the CFTB from $12.5 million to $15 million at the time of the casino opening, though that amount can be higher if 1% of its gross gaming revenue exceeds $15 million.

selection.gap: The verified primary-source passages provided here document a $12.5 million minimum from facility opening, not the $15 million minimum in the question. They also do not directly establish that an independent local board was formally constituted to administer the fund, nor provide evidence of actual opening or payments. A primary Bally’s/CAC amendment or final host-community agreement reflecting the later reported $15 million increase would materially affect the answer.
